info.title: Vixeo
info.description: API de Vixeo : comptes, profils, synchronisation et configuration distante.

get.description:
Called by the app at launch and when it comes back to the foreground, before any sign-in.
`update_required`: the app blocks until the update is installed; `update_available`: it
suggests it once.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Platform of the installed app (`android` also covers Android TV).

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Version name of the installed app ("1.2.0"). Optional: older builds don't send it.

parameters.name: build
parameters.description: Build number of the installed app (`CFBundleVersion` on iOS, `versionCode` on Android).

current_version.description: Version name sent by the app (null for older builds that don't send it).

latest.description: Newest Android release published on GitHub, or null if none yet (always null on iOS).

notes.description: What's new, in French (may be null).

download_url.description: Android: the APK to download and install (https), or null.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the APK, to check before installing (null without APK).

minimum_build.description: Installs older than this build must update: a GitHub release marked « [obligatoire] » (null: none).

update_url.description: Page where the update is installed: the site's install page (no Play Store).

get.description:
`available`: the server has its settings; otherwise the app says the sign-in isn't
available yet, without opening the browser.

post.description:
The code the browser brought back and the secret of the `code_challenge`. Same answer as
`auth/login`, plus `created` (a new account, with its first profile) and `password_removed`
(the account had this address but nobody had ever proved it was theirs: its password and
its other devices were removed).
post.summary: Get a token with the code

token.description: Bearer token to send in the `Authorization` header.

created.description: A new account (and its first profile).

password_removed.description: The account's password and other devices were removed (an address nobody had proved).

get.description:
Opened by the app in a browser: sends it to Google or Apple. A provider the server isn't
set up for sends it straight back to `redirect_uri` with `?error=unavailable`.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description:
Where the browser comes back with the code: `app.vixeo://auth` (Android, iOS) or
`http://127.0.0.1:{port}/auth` (Windows, a server of the app on the device).

parameters.name: code_challenge
parameters.description: PKCE (RFC 7636): base64url of the SHA-256 of a secret the app keeps (`code_verifier`).

get.description:
Called by the provider (Google: GET; Apple: POST, `form_post`), never by the app. Sends the
browser back to the app's `redirect_uri` with `?code=` (5 minutes, once) or `?error=`
(`cancelled`, `failed`, `email`: no address, `unverified`: the provider didn't check the
address of an existing account). A sign-in that has expired gets a page saying so.
get.summary: Come back from Google or Apple (in the browser)

post.description:
202 `{"status":"pending"}` until the code is approved, then 200 with the token (once).
410 when the code expired or was already used: start again.

message.const: Ce code est invalide ou a expiré. Affichez un nouveau code sur la TV.

post.description: Called by the signed-in phone before approving, to show which device asks.
The TV is then signed in to the account of the person approving.

get.description:
Featured carousel (titles with a backdrop) and themed rows.

Items carry their title logo (`logo_url`) and a textless poster, unlike other lists.

After TMDb's curated lists come the trends of the day, then rows by streaming platform, TV
network, studio and language (`list`: `trending_day`, `platform_netflix`, `network_hbo`,
`studio_marvel`, `language_fr`…). Their items carry no logo nor summary. Every row has its
"see all" page: `GET /catalog/{type}/lists/{list}`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only movies or only TV shows. Omit for a mixed home.

parameters.name: X-Profile-Id
parameters.description: Active profile id: its age limit is applied.

active profile's age limit; titles TMDb doesn't know are left out.

returned without a filter.

post.description:
Deletes the account, its profiles, their list, progress and history, and signs out every
device. Cannot be undone. The password is sent in the body (POST, not DELETE: never a
secret in a URL); an account without a password (Google, Apple) sends none.

Confirmed with the account password. The address is used to sign in and to receive the
password reset codes; a pending reset code for the old address is cancelled. 5 tries per
minute (wrong password: 422). An account without a password (Google, Apple) creates one
first (422 on `password`).

Confirmed with the current password. Every other device is signed out; this one stays
signed in. 5 tries per minute (wrong password: 422). An account without a password (created
with Google or Apple, `has_password` false) creates its first one: no `current_password`.

Sends a JSON file with the account, profiles, list, progress and devices to the account's
address (GDPR right of access and portability). Limited to 3 per hour.
post.summary: E-mail a copy of the account's data

get.description:
Messages of the others the active profile has not read, in all its conversations, the
requests it received included: the badge of « Messages » in the apps (« 9+ » above 9).
`requests_count`: requests waiting for an answer.

post.description:
The direct conversation with this member; a new one is a request the member accepts or
declines (until then, only the active profile writes, without attachments).
The active profile runs it (`admin`); 31 members at most.
Neither can write to the other, start a conversation nor add the other to a group.

get.description: For the members of its conversation only.

Its 20 latest messages (oldest first), or the 20 before `before`; `has_more`: older ones
exist. `is_request`: a request the active profile received; `blocked`: it blocked the other
profile of a direct conversation.

those of muted or blocked profiles), and the titles the profiles it follows watched or liked,

tastes in common with their author, their age. Same items as the feed. `page`: 1 first;

get.description:
Items changed since `cursor`, oldest change first. Store the returned `cursor` and
call again while `has_more` is true.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `cursor` returned by the previous pull. 0 (default) = full download.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max items per call (default 500, max 1000). Repeat while `has_more` is true.

cursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` on the next pull.

post.description:
For each group (favorite, progress, watched) the most recent change (`at`) wins.
Returns the merged state of the pushed items. Then pull to get the other devices' changes.

get.description:
The player loads this URL without a bearer token: the signed, opaque token in the path is
what authorises it. An HLS playlist is rewritten so its URIs point back to this server.
get.summary: Media of a channel, proxied (HLS playlist and its segments)

get.description:
The image (PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF), served from our origin: the `logo` URL of a channel.
404 when the provider has no usable image (the app then shows its own icon).
The categories the channels are sorted into (Sport, Cinéma, Info…).
Optionally filtered by category_id, and by a name search with q.

Its name, category and logo (an image on our origin, `GET /tv/logo/{hash}`, from the logo
library, the programme guide or the provider; null when none has one): the channel page of
the app.

The programmes from the one on now, in order (30 at most, the next 48 hours), with UTC
times. `available` is false when the server has no guide; `data` is also empty when the
guide doesn't know the channel, or while it is being downloaded for the first time.

The provider internals stay server-side. The app receives a playlist URL on our own origin
(so it works over HTTPS even when the provider only serves plain HTTP) and no headers: the
player loads the media itself, through the token in the URL.
get.summary: Resolve a playable stream for a channel
